Class 5 · Chapter 6 of 10

Convert and compare measurements

Read scales and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Angles, symmetry, perimeter and area. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can read a dial or thermometer.
  • I can compare mixed units.
  • I can solve a measurement story and estimate sensibly.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Read a dial

Check what each small mark is worth before you read.

This gauge goes from 0 to 20 kg. The needle is on 14.

The mass is 14 kg.

Screen 2 of 4

Convert units

1 km = 1000 m. 1 kg = 1000 g. 1 l = 1000 ml.

To change a big unit to a small unit, multiply by 1000.

12 l 626 ml − 7 l 412 ml: 12,626 ml − 7,412 ml = 5,214 ml.

Screen 3 of 4

Compare in the same unit

Which is greater: 18 l or 17,184 ml?

18 l is 18,000 ml.

18,000 is more than 17,184, so 18 l is greater.

Screen 4 of 4

Choose a sensible unit

Small, light things use grams. Bigger things use kilograms.

A pencil is a few grams.

A school bag is a few kilograms.

Words to know
convert
Change a measurement to another unit with the same size.
capacity
How much a container holds.
estimate
A sensible guess close to the real measurement.

For parents

What your child learns

Convert litres and millilitres by using 1 l = 1000 ml. Scales may have negative numbers, such as -10 up to 40. Subtract all poured amounts from the total in the same unit.

A common slip

Children often mix litres and millilitres. Convert first. On a scale, count the gaps between marks to know what each stands for.

5-minute home activity: Litres and ml

  1. Write 16 l in ml.
  2. Subtract 1822 ml and 3041 ml from it.
  3. Draw a scale and read a reading between marks.
  4. Check by adding back.
